Sales volumes in the third quarter of 2026 averaged 9,559 boe/d as compared to 11,682 boe/d in the third quarter of 2025. Liquids volumes (oil and NGL's) in the third quarter of 2026 averaged 6,489 bbl/d (68%) as compared to 7,254 boe/d (62%) in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in overall volumes reflects the disposition of non-essential assets. Journey closed the disposition of its Countess assets (950 boe/d 100% natural gas) on June 1, 2026 and the disposition of certain Northwest Alberta properties (1,170 boe/d 68% liquids) on September 1.

In aggregate, since 2024, Journey has disposed of approximately 2,950 boe/d (38% liquids) of non-essential assets, where it had no plans to allocate capital over the next five years. This reduced the corporate asset retirement obligations by approximately $87 million. Journey's divestment program is now substantially complete. As Journey replaces divested production with new volumes from drilling, consisting predominantly of Duvernay light oil, Journey is forecasting lower operating expenses per boe, lower royalty as a percentage of revenue, and materially higher netbacks moving forward.

Capital expenditures, before dispositions, in the second quarter of 2026 were $32.9 million, which included $9.2 million for Duvernay facility development, $3.3 million for power, and $3.7 million for land. During the quarter Journey closed on the acquisition of critical infrastructure in the Gilby area. This included acquiring a 0.98% working interest in the Keyera Rimbey gas processing facility. Net acquisition and divestment proceeds for the third quarter were $20 million.

The $3.3 million for power involved commissioning charges associated with ramping up power at the Gilby facility and overhauling the engines at Mazeppa as part of its final completion phase. Power expenditures are largely complete and Journey forecasts much lower quarterly power capital costs moving forward.

In addition to the expanded capital for the Duvernay, Journey also increased facility capital in Cherhill and Skiff by approximately $3 million to fund a number of pipeline integrity projects to ensure reliability of the infrastructure over the long-term. The projects will all be completed within the fourth quarter of 2026.

The timing of future Duvernay pad additions and the phasing of infrastructure capital will continue to result in quarter over quarter variations in production and capital for the Company. In October, Journey added production from 4 gross (1.2 net) Duvernay wells. In November, Journey added production from 1 gross (0.3 net) Duvernay wells. Based on field receipts reports, production for October was 9,965 boe/d (69% liquids) and Journey remains on track to achieving its published year-end guidance.

To date in 2026, Journey has brought on 12 gross (3.0 net) Duvernay wells. Journey forecasts placing on-production another 4 gross (1.2 net) Duvernay wells at the end of the year. Journey's 4.2 net wells brought on-stream in 2026 compares favorably with 2.1 net wells in 2025 and 0.6 net wells in 2024. Significant infrastructure projects in 2026 have paved the way for even higher activity levels in 2027.
At the end of 2026, Journey will have up to 5 gross (1.5 net) drilled and uncompleted wells ("

) off the 10-19-42-3W5 pad to be completed in 2027. These additional wells, along with additional infrastructure and completion costs associated with the 02-22-42-4 pad wells will result in an additional $15 million of capital net to Journey for 2026, which is an increase from previous guidance issued in August. The additional capital represents an acceleration of previously planned 2027 capital into 2026. This will result in higher exit volumes, increased first quarter, 2027 funds flows, and a significant increase in proved, producing reserve additions at the end of the year. The economic strength of the Duvernay resource remains extremely robust and Journey will continue to review and update its program over the course of 2027.
Partial joint venture well drilled across southern border of the play.

The economic viability of the Duvernay play is further substantiated by Journey's realized revenues from wells brought on-production to date. The original two 2024 wells achieved Payout1 in approximately thirteen months at average WTI prices of approximately $64 USD/bbl. The original three wells on the 06-04 pad achieved Payout in approximately thirteen months and the original four wells on the 02-22 pad are forecast to achieve Payout in fourteen to fifteen months.

Journey previously indicated that 2026 capital expenditures in the Duvernay carried a high facility component. Journey participated for its 30% working interest for the construction of a 30 MMcf/d compressor station (in-service), and approximately 25 kilometers of gathering and inter-pad connection pipelines. Journey's net share of these 2026 long-term investments is estimated to be approximately $23 million. The long-term investment in facility projects will benefit the Company for many years by improving cycle times, reducing operating costs, and reducing facility costs for future drilling pads.
Payout means the period of time required for a well or project to generate enough net cash flow to recover its initial capital investment.

Journey achieved Adjusted Funds Flow of $24.3 million during the third quarter of 2026. While average daily sales volumes were 19% lower than the third quarter of 2025, average realized commodity prices were 39% higher than the comparable quarter of 2025 due primarily to a 32% increase in realized crude oil prices. Realized crude oil prices rose to $103.87/bbl in the third quarter resulting primarily from the continuation of the US-Iran war. The spike in WTI oil prices had a positive impact on Adjusted Funds Flow which was partially offset by a $3.8 million loss related from oil hedging.

Journey's overall liquids (crude oil and NGL's) volume weighting continued to strengthen with its Duvernay drilling results and the disposition of natural gas assets in June. Liquids volumes increased to 68% of total volumes in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to 61% in the third quarter of 2025. Crude oil sales volumes for the third quarter of 2026 represented 56%, an increase from 50% in the third quarter of 2025. Oil revenues represented 88% of total revenues in the third quarter of 2026. Natural gas sales volumes contributed 32% of total boe volumes in the third quarter of 2026 while contributing only 4% of total sales revenues. This weighting dynamic is the direct result of Journey's initiative to increase its corporate light oil weighting.

Journey's operating netbacks were $35.47/boe in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to $20.68 in the third quarter of 2025. 39% higher average commodity prices between the two comparable quarters in 2026 and 2025, along with Journey's changing product mix were the primary drivers of the increase.

Journey generated net income of $16.8 million in the third quarter of 2026 or $0.25 per basic share and $0.24 per diluted share as compared to $4.4 million of net income in the third quarter of 2025 or $0.07 per basic share and $0.06 per diluted share. Included in third quarter, 2026 net income was $7.0 million for a mark-to-market hedging loss and a further $3.8 million of realized hedging losses. The realized hedging losses were primarily attributable to the significant spike in WTI oil prices in relation to the fixed price. Adjusted Funds Flow of $24.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, was 19% higher than the $20.5 million realized in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted Funds Flow per share was $0.36 per basic weighted average share and $0.35 per diluted share for the third quarter of 2026 as compared to $0.30 per basic weighted average and diluted share in the third quarter of 2025.

Net capital expenditures for the third quarter of 2026 includes exploration and development expenditures of $32.9 million and disposition proceeds of $28 million. $25.8 million was spent on drilling, completion, equipping and tie-in costs that were primarily devoted to Duvernay development activities including drilling 7 (2.1 net) new wells. In addition, the Company spent $3.3 million on the continuing work on its power generation projects in Gilby and Mazeppa. Journey spent $8 million in the acquisition of a 0.98% working interest in the Keyera Rimbey natural gas processing facility and associated infrastructure. The working interest generates third party processing revenue of approximately $0.7 million per year, but more significantly, the acquisition is expected to deliver a net reduction in operating expenses for processing Journey's working interest natural gas production from the Duvernay joint venture. Journey exited the third quarter of 2026 with net debt of $48.4 million, which was 13% lower than the $55.4 million at the end of the third quarter of 2025 and 4% lower than the $50.6 million of net debt at the beginning of the year.

Journey has updated its 2026 capital spending and production guidance as per below. The Company has increased its capital spending plans from the previous guidance, accelerated the on-stream date for the 02-22 pad wells, accelerated facility capital from 2027 into 2026, and added capital for the first five wells of the 10-19 pad. Capital has been reduced in 2027 to reflect the acceleration of capital into 2026.

Sales volumes for 2026 were reduced to reflect the loss of the Countess volumes effective June 1, 2026 (950 boe/d, 100% natural gas) and the Northwest Alberta volumes (1,170 boe/d, 32% natural gas) sold effective September 1, 2026.

Journey is maintaining its 2026 exit volumes, however it anticipates a significant production increase when the 4 gross (1.2 net) 02-22 pad wells come on-production in January of 2027. The robust economic impact of volume additions from the Duvernay continues to be reinforced with every new pad brought on-stream.

Journey is in the strongest position in its history to capitalize on the opportunity created by its world class Duvernay resource. Under current pricing assumptions, Journey has sufficient capital and liquidity available to fully fund its capital program. Journey management looks forward to providing further updates to this guidance at regular intervals throughout the year and as circumstances change.

is calculated by taking "cash flow provided by operating activities" from the financial statements and adding or deducting: changes in non-cash working capital; non-recurring "other" income; transaction costs; and decommissioning costs. Adjusted Funds Flow per share is calculated as Adjusted Funds Flow divided by the weighted-average number of shares outstanding in the period. Because Adjusted Funds Flow and Adjusted Funds Flow per share are not impacted by fluctuations in non-cash working capital balances, Management believes these measures are more indicative of performance than the GAAP measured "cash flow generated from operating activities". In addition, Journey excludes transaction costs from the definition of Adjusted Funds Flow, as these expenses are generally in respect of capital acquisition transactions. The Company considers Adjusted Funds Flow a key performance measure as it demonstrates the Company's ability to generate funds necessary to repay debt and to fund future growth through capital investment.
